turns.doctor_question: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, hi. Um, I guess I’m here because... well, it’s been getting to the point where I just, I feel like I can’t settle in my own body anymore. I mean, it’s really hard to explain, but it’s like this constant hum, and I just can't get comfortable. Since I'm not working right now—I have my bachelor's degree, but I've been out of the workforce for a bit—I have all these things I'm supposed to be managing for the house. 

And it's just... especially when I’m supposed to sit quietly and handle the paperwork, or when we need to go over shared household plans, I just can't do it. I sit down at the kitchen table with the bills or the schedules, and my foot starts tapping, and I feel this intense urge to just get up and do literally anything else. I’ll think, oh, I should wipe down the counters first, or I need to check the mail, or maybe I should reorganize the pantry, and it's just exhausting. My body physically rejects the idea of sitting still for it. It's like my skin is crawling if I have to just be quiet and sit there for more than two minutes, and it's really starting to become a huge problem for me.

turns.doctor_question: Did you experience this kind of restlessness or difficulty sitting still when you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, gosh, yes. I mean, if I really think about it... looking back, this was absolutely already a part of me way back in elementary school. I just... I didn't realize what it was back then, obviously, and I don't think my parents did either. But I was definitely that girl. You know, the one with the completely messy desk where everything was just shoved inside? Just a disaster of crumpled up papers and broken crayons. 

My mom used to get so incredibly frustrated with me because of the forgotten permission slips. I was always either leaving them on the kitchen counter, or losing them in the black hole of my backpack until they were three weeks overdue and completely shredded. It was a whole production every time a field trip came around. 

And the parent-teacher conferences... oh, they were always exactly the same. Every single year, my parents would get these notes from my teachers saying that I talked out of turn, just constantly blurting things out because I couldn't hold the thought in my head, or that I seemed completely unable to stay seated. I’d always be up sharpening my pencil, or walking to the trash can, or just... standing by my chair for no reason. I remember my third-grade teacher actually got so exhausted by it that she made me the "door monitor" just so I had a sanctioned excuse to get up and walk across the room, because otherwise I was just popping up out of my seat every five minutes anyway. It wasn't that I wanted to be bad or disruptive, I just... I physically couldn't stay put. My legs just had to move. So, yeah, it’s been there pretty much my whole life, even if people just thought I was a chatterbox or a messy kid back then.
